title: Teachers in Space Plans to Send Two Educators on 2027 Research Flight with Virgin Galactic
summary: Nonprofit launches campaign to fund its full educational program, including a classroom-designed research space mission
body_markdown:
NEW YORK, November 18, 2026 — Teachers in Space (TIS), a nonprofit that trains teachers to design, build, and fly real space experiments, today announced plans to send two teachers to space aboard a Virgin Galactic research flight expected in 2027.


TIS teachers have conducted research in microgravity on parabolic “zero-G” flights since 2016. This mission is expected to be the first time TIS teachers conduct research in space themselves.


“Our mission is to fly people whose work in space will make a difference back on Earth, and few people carry that impact further than teachers. These educators plan to conduct research in space and then bring it into their classrooms, where it can shape how the next generation of scientists and engineers sees what’s possible,” said Mike Moses, President, Spaceline, Virgin Galactic.


The TIS team is working to raise $2 million to support this educational program and research mission. The campaign is off to a strong start, with $285,000 raised to date.


**A Proven Blueprint: From Classroom to Flight and Back**


The mission builds on a model TIS has refined over more than a decade: Teachers build a 3D-printed CubeSat—which measures 3.5. by 3.5 inches—and is powered by a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery. Each CubeSat pairs an Arduino microcontroller with a suite of environmental sensors measuring temperature, pressure, acceleration, rotation (gyroscope), magnetic field, carbon dioxide, humidity and light, with a real-time clock time-stamping every reading. Teachers then fly the CubeSat.


The data returns to the K-12 classrooms that designed their teachers’ experiments, and students can analyze how conditions changed from launch through weightlessness and back to landing.


To date, TIS has trained more than 800 teachers, bringing space education to an estimated 70,000 students. “Putting a teacher in space is the natural evolution of our program,” said Liz Kennick, CEO of Teachers in Space.


**Extending Space Access to Teachers and Students**


TIS’s experiments are already providing real-world results. One sophomore high school student developed a radiation-sensing experiment to test a material that could potentially be used to protect humans traveling beyond Earth’s magnetic field. TIS has flown that experiment to the upper atmosphere and space on various flight platforms. That student went on to complete a PhD in engineering.


For many participants, the lasting result is confidence. “I have learned a lot and gained confidence in my ability to lead students in designing and building their own CubeSats in the months and years to come,” said Wendy Agnes of Indooroopilly State High School in Australia, who attended the August 2026 workshop in New York City.


TIS was created to fulfill the promise of NASA’s original Teacher in Space program, which selected Christa McAuliffe from more than 11,000 applicants to serve as the first teacher in space in 1985.


**About Teachers in Space**


Teachers in Space is a 501(c)(3) dedicated to providing STEM education to teachers, as well as hands-on experience and industry contacts. For more information, see[tis.org](http://tis.org/) . To donate, please visit[the GiveButter fundraising page](https://givebutter.com/fund-stem-training-for-100-educators-s14sb0) .
